stories.headline: Nepal flash floods: MEA sets up round-the-clock control room in Delhi
stories.title: Nepal flash floods: MEA sets up round-the-clock control room in Delhi
stories.summary: New Delhi, Aug 27: In view of the flood situation in Nepal, the Ministry of External Affairs has set up a round-the-clock control room here to assist people. As the death toll from Nepal's devastating flash floods surged to 359 on Thursday, rescuers launched a race against time to trace hundreds still missing, including 288 Indian nationals. “We have set up a control room in the Ministry of External Affairs here, which will function round-the-clock. Details of the helpline and the control room telephone numbers are being put out on our X handle, and you should be getting them soon. Our embassies, both in Kathmandu and in Beijing, have also set up 24x7 helplines,” ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at a media briefing here. Later, the MEA shared details of the control room in a statement. “The control room can be contacted at +91 11 2308 8718 +91 11 2308 8719. For WhatsApp calls/messages: +91 9968291988. Email: situationroom@mea.gov.in,” it said. The emergency contact numbers of the Indian embassy in Kathmandu are (also on WhatsApp): +977 985 131 6807; +977 970 910 7500; and +977 981 032 6117. The massive flash floods originating in Tibet swept through central Nepal on Wednesday, devastating several towns and villages, washing away critical bridges and crippling a dozen hydropower projects, affecting multiple districts. India on Thursday said it stands “shoulder-to-shoulder” with Nepal to help it deal with the crisis as rescue operations gathered momentum in the Himalayan nation. According to the MEA, Nepali authorities can be contacted at the following helpline numbers: Tourist Police: +977 9851289445; Nepal Army: +977 9851072914 (email: dgmi-foreign@nepalarmy.mil.np); NDRRMA: +977 9851320269 /+977 9849281097; Rasuwa Police: +977 9851254960; Assistant chief district officer, Rasuwa: +977 9851164422; Nuwakot Police: +977 9851282380; Assistant chief district officer, Nuwakot: +977 9851248777; Dhading Police: +977 9851229860; Chief district officer, Dhading: +977 9851247777; Chitwan Police: +977 9855013999; Assistant chief district officer, Chitwan: +977 9855088891.

stories.headline: What a 132-yr-old Himalayan disaster can teach us about Nepal flash floods
stories.title: What a 132-yr-old Himalayan disaster can teach us about Nepal flash floods
stories.summary: The 1894 Gohna Lake disaster shows how early warnings can save lives even when the Himalayas cannot be tamed
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The devastating flash flood that struck Nepal’s Rasuwa district on the morning of Wednesday, 26 August was a reminder of how quickly the Himalayas can turn from a source of life into an agent of destruction.
Water, sediment and huge boulders raced through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems, devastating settlements and infrastructure.
Preliminary assessments by scientists suggest that an ice-rock avalanche may have fallen into the Lhende Khola, a tributary of the Bhote Koshi, triggering the sudden surge.
The speed was extraordinary.
At Galchhi, downstream on the Trishuli, the river level reportedly rose by as much as nine metres in just 30 minutes.
Scientists are also examining whether avalanche debris temporarily blocked the river, creating the possibility of another sudden release downstream.
There is little humans can do to prevent such geological events.
But they can understand the hazard, monitor it, communicate warnings and move people out of harm’s way.
That lesson was demonstrated spectacularly — not by satellites or artificial intelligence, but by engineers, geologists and administrators more than 130 years ago in the Garhwal Himalayas.
On 21 September 1893, a massive landslide blocked the Birehi Ganga, a tributary of the Alaknanda, in present-day Uttarakhand.
The landslide came down from a high mountain slope, creating a gigantic natural dam.
Behind it, water accumulated to form what became known as Gohna Lake.

stories.headline: Gurugram’s Monsoon Crisis: Garbage-Choked Badshahpur Drain Turns Millennium City Into Flood Zone
stories.title: Gurugram’s Monsoon Crisis: Garbage-Choked Badshahpur Drain Turns Millennium City Into Flood Zone
stories.summary: Gurugram is India’s Millennium City — home to massive investments, corporate hubs and some of the country’s biggest companies. But when the monsoon arrives, a different Gurugram emerges. India Today investigates the Badshahpur Drain, one of the city’s crucial drainage channels, and finds stretches clogged with garbage and hardened silt, severely restricting water flow. From Tulip Chowk to Vatika Chowk and Badshahpur, the investigation tracks the growing bottleneck and asks a crucial question: why does a city that attracts billions in investment continue to struggle with basic drainage and desilting? As heavy rains return, the consequences are visible on Gurugram’s roads, residential areas and daily life.

stories.headline: J&K Deputy CM says Congress likely to join government soon, attacks BJP over ‘discrimination’ against Jammu
stories.title: J&K Deputy CM says Congress likely to join government soon, attacks BJP over ‘discrimination’ against Jammu
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 27: Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary said on Thursday that the Congress is expected to join the National Conference-led government soon, describing the move as a natural development given the two parties’ alliance. Choudhary said the National Conference had wanted Congress to become part of the government since the alliance was formed, but that the final decision had rested with the Congress. “As far as Congress is concerned, ever since this government was formed, when we entered into the alliance, it was our desire and we wanted Congress to join,” he said. “But Congress was unable to take a decision. Now Congress is taking a decision, and I think everyone should be happy because it is an alliance partner.” He said Congress joining the government would strengthen the administration and help it deliver for the people. “If Congress also comes in, the government will run with greater strength and we will be able to work for the people,” Choudhary said. “Because it is our alliance partner, they have a right to come into the government.” Asked what the National Conference was offering Congress, including the number of ministerial berths, Choudhary rejected the suggestion that the party was negotiating through inducements. “We are not BJP people. We are not like the BJP people who do horse-trading,” he said. “These are relationships of the heart. We are people who connect hearts, and decisions taken from the heart last long and are for the betterment of the people.” He added: “It does not happen that we will bring someone by giving them greed or temptation. This is the work of the BJP.” Deputy CM attacks BJP over Jammu ‘discrimination’ Choudhary also launched a broadside against the BJP, accusing it of failing to address what he described as discrimination against Jammu. Responding to BJP claims that a cabinet reshuffle could bring down the government, he said the BJP should focus instead on issues affecting the region. He questioned why, according to him, there was no Jammu-based professor serving as vice-chancellor at any of Jammu’s universities and why no local doctor had become director of AIIMS. “Is this not discrimination that professors and doctors from Jammu do not have the right to become vice-chancellors or directors?” he asked. “Are our professors so incompetent? Are our doctors so incompetent that they cannot become vice-chancellors? Can they not become directors of AIIMS, IIM or IIT?” He urged the media in Jammu to question the BJP on these issues rather than focus on the National Conference. “Tell them not to talk about things here and there. Tell them why discrimination against Jammu is still not ending,” he said. Choudhary also alleged that Jammu’s business sector was suffering and challenged the BJP to explain how it planned to revive trade and industry in the region. He referred to the ₹28,000-crore industrial package for Jammu and Kashmir and questioned whether existing industries in Jammu had benefited from it. “Go to the Gangyal Industrial Estate, go to Bari Brahmana Industrial Estate, go to Samba, go to Kathua and wherever our industrial estates are,” he said. “Ask whether the old industries of Jammu and Kashmir have received anything from the package. Nothing has been given.” Power tariffs, inflation and cost of living The Deputy Chief Minister also defended the government on electricity tariffs, arguing that the issue should be viewed against the record of the previous BJP-PDP administration. “You should compare the last 12 years,” he said. “Find out how much electricity rates increased during the BJP period and how high electricity bills were.” He also pointed to the government’s electricity amnesty measures and challenged the BJP to answer questions about the rising prices of basic commodities. “Ask the BJP people how much sugar costs. Is it ₹70 or ₹75 a kilo?” he said. “Ask them how much pulses cost. Ask them the price of vegetables and onions.” Choudhary said the impact of inflation was particularly severe on ordinary households. “For a poor man who has only one bulb, what does he know whether the bill is bigger or smaller?” he said. “He knows the price of the sugar he needs for his tea.” He also accused the BJP of failing to address rising education and healthcare costs. “Ask them why fees in universities have increased,” he said. “Ask them about the fees in hospitals. These are important issues.” ‘We will take back Article 370 and statehood’ On Article 370 and statehood, Choudhary said the National Conference remained committed to restoring Jammu and Kashmir’s special status and statehood. “We will take back 370. We will take back special status. We will protect our children’s jobs and will not allow our poor people’s land to be taken by outsiders,” he said. He argued that the BJP had itself made commitments regarding employment and land during the parliamentary debate following the 2019 changes. “This was a promise made by the BJP,” Choudhary said. “It was said in Parliament that the jobs of Jammu and Kashmir would not be taken by outsiders and the land of the people of Jammu and Kashmir would not be taken by outsiders.” He said the BJP therefore had an even greater responsibility to address the issues of special status and statehood. ‘Stop counting the sacrifices of children’ Choudhary also criticised BJP leader Ashok Kaul over remarks concerning the number of BJP children who had died during militancy. He said the deaths of young people should not be turned into a political calculation. “A child may belong to a poor family, a child may be a BJP worker’s child, a child may be from the National Conference, PDP, Congress or any other party, or even an ordinary person’s child—if someone is killed in militancy, it is a matter of great sorrow,” he said. “What kind of counting is this that you have started, Ashok Kaul sahib?” he asked. He also questioned BJP leaders over their participation, or that of their children, in the Ram temple movement and said political leaders should stop comparing sacrifices. “Stop talking about the sacrifices and martyrdom of children,” he said, urging the BJP to instead answer questions about Jammu and Kashmir. BJP challenged over unemployment and vacant posts Choudhary further challenged the BJP to explain its record on unemployment and the regularisation of temporary workers. Ahead of the BJP’s proposed September 2 protest at the Civil Secretariat, he asked the party to explain why vacant posts had not been filled over the past 12 years. “Ask them why they did not fill them,” he said, referring to vacant government posts. He also questioned why various categories of temporary workers—including SPOs, Home Guards, daily wagers and workers associated with horticulture, agriculture and other departments—had not been regularised. “They talk about unemployment. Ask them, you had promised that you would provide two crore jobs,” Choudhary said. “Of that two crore, what share did Jammu and Kashmir get?” He also invoked the BJP’s earlier promise of depositing ₹15 lakh in people’s bank accounts, saying the party should fulfil that promise before coming to the Civil Secretariat. ‘We are politicians; we move towards the destination’ On speculation about internal divisions within the National Conference and whether political developments could affect the party, Choudhary said his focus remained on fulfilling the commitments made to the people. “We are politicians. We move towards the destination,” he said. “We do not calculate into plus or minus. We know that the destination is in front of us, and that destination is one—to work for the welfare of the people and fulfil the promises we have made.” Choudhary also dismissed suggestions that he was afraid of the BJP, pointing out that he had previously defeated its state president. “If I was afraid of the BJP, I would not have left after defeating its state president,” he said.

article_sentences: Kotak Mahindra Investments Ltd.
has appointed Hiren Vora as its chief financial officer and key managerial personnel, effective September 1, 2026, following the resignation of Siddarth Gandotra.
The company’s board, at a meeting Thursday, noted Gandotra’s resignation as CFO and key managerial personnel, effective at the close of business on August 31.
The board subsequently approved Vora’s appointment from the following day.
Gandotra will continue in his role through August 31 before Vora takes charge, ensuring an immediate transition in the company’s finance leadership.
Kotak Mahindra Investments disclosed the changes under the Securities and Exchange Board of India’s listing regulations.
Details relating to Gandotra and Vora were included in annexures accompanying the regulatory filing.

Hiren Vora will take over as chief financial officer from September 1, following Siddarth Gandotra’s resignation at the end of August.

stories.headline: India, China, Canada & more: 10 countries still under Trump’s tariff squeeze and why
stories.title: India, China, Canada & more: 10 countries still under Trump’s tariff squeeze and why
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: From India and Canada to Iran and Venezuela, the countries may be thousands of miles apart and have little in common economically.

Yet they have found themselves facing the same problem: an unpredictable US trade policy under President Donald Trump, in which tariffs and sanctions are being deployed for reasons that go beyond conventional trade disputes.

Trade deficits remain a key justification for many measures, but Trump has increasingly tied economic pressure to wars, Russian oil, fentanyl, immigration, deportations, drug trafficking, nuclear programmes and even the domestic policies of US allies.

That sequence of threaten, negotiate, delay, collapse talks, retaliate and threaten further escalation has become a defining feature of Trump's approach, making the tariff regime difficult for governments and businesses to predict.
Canada has emerged as one of the clearest and most recently escalated examples of how Trump's trade policy has expanded beyond trade.

In the latest, Ottawa announced 15 per cent, 25 per cent and 50 per cent retaliatory tariffs on C$27.6 billion of US goods, effective September 8, matching Washington's measures “dollar for dollar, rate for rate.”
The tariffs cover steel, dairy, seafood, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, electronics and other goods.
Canada also announced a C$7.5 billion support package for affected workers and businesses.
The move followed Trump's 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian goods after trade talks collapsed.
But the dispute has long involved more than trade.
In 2025, Trump repeatedly cited fentanyl trafficking and illegal immigration, accusing Ottawa of failing to secure the northern border, while also alleging discriminatory treatment of US products.
The negotiations brought in another non-trade issue.
